definition.description: A trim on the input BEFORE the analysis, in decibels: 0 leaves it alone, +6 doubles it, +20 is ten times. Every channel the session publishes (level, the bands, the spectrum, onset, the hit counts, the tonal nodes) is measured on the trimmed signal. Raise it for a quiet input: the bands are a window from -100 to -30 dB, so a microphone hearing speakers across a room sits at the floor, and nothing downstream can recover what the analyser never saw. Lower it for a hot one: past full scale level stops at 1 and a band stops at 1, so the peaks flatten. Watch level and the bands while you set it. A value like any other, so drive it, store it in a preset or put it on a Panel; a change is ramped over a few hundredths of a second and never restarts the capture. A live input is not monitored, so this changes nothing you hear.
definition.label: Input Gain (dB)

definition.description: Monitoring level. Does NOT touch the analysis — the channels report the file at the level Input Gain (Analysis) sets, unity by default, however loud you are playing it, so turning the room down does not silently rescale everything driven by it.
definition.label: Volume

definition.description: A trim on the file BEFORE the analysis, in decibels: 0 leaves it alone, +6 doubles it, +20 is ten times. Every channel is measured on the trimmed file, so a quiet master can be lifted off the floor of the bands' -100 to -30 dB window and a hot one brought back under it (past full scale level stops at 1 and a band stops at 1). It does NOT touch what you hear or the sound an export carries: Volume is the monitor level and does not touch the analysis, this is the analysis level and does not touch the monitor. Read at rest, like Hit Threshold: changing it restarts the capture and re-analyses the file, and an offline render reads the same stored number.
definition.label: Input Gain (dB)
